clue.text: Rod, pole, but plainly not perch

definitions.text: Rod, pole, but plainly not perch

parts.words: Rod, pole, but plainly not perch
parts.note: a long wooden shaft, the thing in the saying 'as plain as a ...'; a perch is also a rod or pole as a length, and a pike is a fish that is not a perch

explanation.surface: Someone sorting fishing gear and fussily insisting this rod is not the perch kind.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'as plain as a pikestaff' is behind 'plainly'. 'Perch' can be a fish or a measure of length also called a rod or pole; the pike is a fish but not a perch.
explanation.definitionFit: A pikestaff is the wooden shaft of a pike, a kind of rod or pole.

clue.text: One graduate black-belt in Nigeria

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree holder
a dan is a black-belt grade in judo and karate

explanation.surface: A Nigerian martial arts expert with a university degree.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a place found in Nigeria.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibadan is a large city in south-western Nigeria, so it is a place there.

clue.text: Close to a conclusion

parts.note: read both as near the end and as the closing part itself

explanation.surface: A story nearly finished.
explanation.definitionFit: An ending is the final part or conclusion of something, and something ending is near its close.

clue.text: Lowest form of cleaners

indicators.note: the letters are given a different form, a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A remark that cleaners are the humblest workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' signals an anagram of LOWEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Towels are cloths used for drying and wiping, so they clean.

clue.text: Fresh in-patient?

definitions.meaning: a hospital patient is one admitted for a bed in a hospital room

explanation.surface: A cheeky hospital patient.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as FOR WARD, it describes a patient being admitted to a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: A forward person is overly bold, and an in-patient is someone bound for a ward.

clue.text: They must be given a lead

definitions.text: They must be given a lead

parts.words: They must be given a lead
parts.note: reads like dogs on leashes, but means people who need someone to lead them

explanation.surface: Dogs that must be kept on leashes.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers are disciples or supporters, who look to a leader to guide them.

clue.text: Disowned tearabout member of the cat family

indicators.note: the torn word goes about the cat, surrounding it

parts.note: to rend is to tear apart
the ounce is another name for the snow leopard

explanation.surface: A disowned hooligan who is something of a big cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tearabout' is printed as one word but parses as 'tear' with the container signal 'about'. The cat is the snow leopard, also called the ounce.
explanation.definitionFit: To renounce is to give up or repudiate, so renounced means rejected.

clue.text: Yes, petrol can be absorbed by this material

indicators.note: the letters can be turned into another word when rearranged

explanation.surface: A fabric that soaks up fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' signals an anagram of YES and PETROL.
explanation.definitionFit: Polyester is a synthetic fibre used to make fabric.

clue.text: Jacket the French king has a disapproving cry about

indicators.note: the cry is placed round the other letters, so it goes about them

parts.note: boo is the jeer of disapproval
le is French for the
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A French king being booed while wearing a particular jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places the French article and king between the second and third letters of the jeer; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolero is a short open jacket ending above the waist.

clue.text: Sounds the manicurist's doing

parts.note: spoken, the word sounds like 'handy work', and a manicurist's work is on hands

explanation.surface: A remark on what a manicurist does all day.
explanation.walkthrough: Said out loud, the word sounds like 'handy work', and a manicurist works on hands; the word itself means something a person has done.
explanation.definitionFit: Handiwork is something a person has made or done, so it is their doing.

clue.text: Anything but happy with my new logo

indicators.note: the letters are made into something new, a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A designer who hates the new logo they have been given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' signals an anagram of MY plus LOGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloomy means dejected and low-spirited, the opposite of cheerful.

clue.text: Gem one can learn about

indicators.note: the letters are moved about into a different order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An invitation to study a precious stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals an anagram of I (one), CAN and LEARN.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnelian is a reddish semi-precious stone, a kind of chalcedony.

clue.text: Conflicting family on TV giving new heart to flappers

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter

parts.note: wings are what flap when a bird flies

explanation.surface: A feuding television family that gives birds a fresh core.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ewings were the feuding oil family in the US soap Dallas. 'new heart' reads as a repair, but it is the middle letter of 'new'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ewings were the warring family at the centre of the TV drama Dallas.

clue.text: Ready-made for a golfer's opening drive

definitions.meaning: clothes bought ready to wear, not tailored
a first shot struck from the tee, the small peg holding the ball

explanation.surface: Ready-to-wear clothes fit for a golfer's first shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes bought off the peg are ready to wear; a golfer drives the opening shot from a tee peg.

clue.text: Neat in a spirited way

definitions.meaning: of a drink, served with no water or mixer

explanation.surface: A tidy, lively manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like tidy, but here it means a drink with no water added.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat whisky is unmixed, and spirit drunk that way is unwatered.

clue.text: Dicey operator in the sports business?

definitions.meaning: a crook running a dishonest business
someone involved with bats used in tennis and squash

explanation.surface: A shady character working in sports.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading makes the word someone in the trade of tennis and squash bats.
explanation.definitionFit: A racketeer runs a fraudulent business, and a racket is also a tennis or squash bat.

clue.text: She's a state prosecuting officer, apparently

parts.note: a DA is a district attorney, the US state prosecutor

explanation.surface: Introducing a woman who works as a state prosecutor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apparently' warns that the name looks like A DA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ada is a woman's name, so it can stand for a she.

clue.text: Garment worn in ecclesiastical buildings

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words across their join

explanation.surface: A vestment worn in churches.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the join in ecclesiastical buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: An alb is a long white vestment worn by clergy.

clue.text: A spot of good service at Wimbledon

definitions.meaning: a playing card with one pip

explanation.surface: Praise for a fine serve at the tennis championship.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London tennis championship; the one of a card suit carries a single spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The one in a suit of cards has a single pip, and a serve the opponent cannot touch scores outright.

clue.text: Flier in a flat spin

indicators.note: a spin sends the letters whirling into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone in a panic inside their apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spin' signals an anagram of IN A FLAT; 'in a flat spin' is a phrase for panicking.
explanation.definitionFit: A fantail is a pigeon with a fan-shaped tail, a bird that flies.

clue.text: The last train, perhaps

parts.note: not a final railway service but the line of mourners following someone on their final journey

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether this is the final train home.
explanation.definitionFit: A cortege is a funeral procession, a train of mourners at a last parting.

clue.text: Comb manufacturer

parts.note: not a maker of hair combs but the insect that builds honeycomb

explanation.surface: A firm that makes hair combs.
explanation.definitionFit: Bees build honeycomb from wax, so the insect makes combs.

clue.text: Mince pie followed by fish and fruit topping!

indicators.note: mincing chops up, so the letters are cut and remixed

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A recipe of mince pie with fish and fruit on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mince' signals an anagram of PIE, giving EPI.
explanation.definitionFit: The epicarp is the outer skin of a fruit, the layer covering it.

clue.text: Dupes bridge-players look for

definitions.meaning: the rounds of cards that card players try to win

explanation.surface: Card players hunting for gullible victims.
explanation.definitionFit: To trick is to dupe someone; in bridge, each round of four cards won is counted as one.

clue.text: Hit out in front of leading lady and steal away

indicators.note: the word is knocked out of shape, so its letters move

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: Someone lashing out at the star actress and then sneaking off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' signals that the letters of 'Hit' are jumbled; 'in front of' only fixes their place before the first woman of Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: To thieve is to rob or take what is not yours.

clue.text: Put an end to strong drink

explanation.surface: Giving up hard liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a rumour is to quash it, and Scotch is whisky.

clue.text: Matador's cape raised at the stubborn beast

parts.note: a mule is proverbially obstinate

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word lifts it up and so reads it backwards

explanation.surface: A bullfighter waving his cape at a stubborn animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns AT into TA in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A muleta is the red cloth on a stick a bullfighter uses in the final stage.

clue.text: Another thing, it goes with a swing after dark

definitions.text: Another thing, it goes with a swing after dark

parts.words: Another thing, it goes with a swing after dark
parts.note: a golfer's stick goes with a swing, and night is after dark; a lively late venue also swings

explanation.surface: Something that swings into action once evening falls.
explanation.walkthrough: A golf club 'goes with a swing', and here it is one that swings at night: a lively venue for dancing late.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub is a venue for drinking and dancing that opens late in the evening.

clue.text: Justice resolving quite an unknown factor

indicators.note: the letters are being resolved, sorted out into a new order

parts.note: y is one of the letters used for an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: A judge settling a case and a mysterious element remains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolving' signals an anagram of QUITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Equity is fairness and impartiality, the quality of being just.

clue.text: Compilation concocted by that geezer short of breath

indicators.note: something concocted is cooked up, a mixture made from the letters
breath is the aspirate h sound, so H is taken out

explanation.surface: A book thrown together by some breathless old man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of breath' drops the H (the breathy aspirate) from THAT GEEZER, leaving TATGEEZER; 'concocted' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazetteer is a geographical dictionary or index, a compiled reference list of places.

clue.text: County town stemming from a variety of tree

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of or from

indicators.note: a variety is a different version, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A town said to take its name from a kind of tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a variety of' signals an anagram of TREE, giving ETER. EXETER is the county town of Devon, in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeter is the administrative seat of the English county of Devon.

clue.text: Time for talking of prizes at school

definitions.text: Time for talking of prizes at school

parts.words: Time for talking of prizes at school
parts.note: an occasion of addresses, a day of talking, when a school hands out its awards

explanation.surface: The school day when awards are announced amid lots of talk.
explanation.walkthrough: A school's annual prize-giving, with talks by guests and the head, is called its speech day in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech day is the yearly school occasion when prizes are presented and addresses given.
